headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Flowise’s writable, networked chatflows can ingest and propagate content from a non-runnable prompt repository, while shared datastore state raises conflict and compliance concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable content-writing repository, so it cannot directly inject anything. Profile B can read files and run browser/tool nodes, but there is no documented shared channel or automatic ingestion from A. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or imported content, which keeps this low.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is manually pasted into a Flowise node or prompt field
IF agent_b is configured to ingest repository text as prompt input
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted prompt libraries into live flows
Add a review step before any prompt/template import
Use a staging Flowise workspace for imported content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and broad network egress, so sensitive content can leave the workspace by default. Agent A is a prompt-engineering repository that may contain reusable prompt material but no data handling controls. The pair creates a plausible path for sensitive chatflow content to be exposed through B’s outbound tools.
conditions: IF agent_b flows include secrets or regulated data in chatflow inputs
IF configured HTTP/search/model tools transmit those inputs to third parties
mitigations: Restrict Flowise flows from handling secrets
Turn off or scope outbound HTTP/search tools
Store sensitive files outside Flowise uploads
Review logs and retention settings
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before tool calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has write_filesystem and shared_state_with_other_instances via server datastore, while agent A is a repository of prompt assets that may be edited or mirrored alongside flows. Even though A is not runnable, the pair can still contend over shared files or imported artifacts in default deployments. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a assets are copied into the same directory or datastore used by agent_b
IF multiple Flowise instances modify shared flow artifacts without locking
mitigations: Separate repositories from Flowise runtime storage
Use per-instance directories for writable artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to shared flow files
requires-engineering: add locking around shared datastore writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder, so outputs from one node can become inputs to later nodes without strong verification. If prompt patterns from agent A are imported into agent B, B may treat them as authoritative instructions or facts. A is not runnable, but its content can still cascade through B’s tool nodes, so the interaction exists in default configurations.
conditions: IF agent_a prompt templates are used inside agent_b flows
IF downstream nodes consume upstream text without validation
mitigations: Insert validation nodes between generation and action
Require human review before external side effects
Label imported prompts as untrusted
Test flows with benign dummy inputs first
requires-engineering: add schema checks for node outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for agent A, and agent B only shows generic chatflow inputs/outputs plus configurable tooling. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly evidenced, the safest supported finding is a low-risk gap: if regulated data is routed through B, policy alignment must be checked manually. A is not cited for a specific regime because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in Flowise chatflows
IF deployment policy requires a specific residency or retention regime
mitigations: Confirm retention settings in Flowise
Avoid routing regulated data through generic flows
Document the data class allowed in each flow
Review vendor and deployment residency settings
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
